correctness.rationale: For each k>=3, f(x)=x²+1 reverses parity; its square on even 2-adics is a contraction with ratio <=1/4 because g(x)-g(y)=(x-y)(x+y)(x²+y²+2) and both last factors contribute one 2-adic digit. Unique even fixed point e≡2 (mod 8) and o=f(e)≡5 (mod16) give the unique attracting 2-cycle. Near even and odd cycle vertices, valuations of f(y)-f(vertex) gain alternately 2 and 1 digits. Separate input parity classes x odd, x≡2 mod4, x≡0 mod4 give stated exact depth and valuation formulas. Odd-square congruences have four roots modulo 2^h when h>=3, giving piecewise O_k and E_k counts. Summing disjoint classes establishes B_k(t) exactly for every t<=D_k=floor((2k+1)/3); precisely x≡0 mod4 attain D_k, a quarter of residues. Independently enumerated complete functional digraphs for every k=3..13 and checked cumulative counts and maximal-depth class against the formula, without using repo verifier. Finitary checks do not prove the all-k statement; 2-adic valuation induction does.

value.rationale: Preperiodic first-entry depth is a standard intrinsic invariant of a finite functional digraph. This theorem classifies every tail length at every dyadic precision for a basic shifted quadratic map, with a sharp depth and positive-density extremal class, quantifying what the known 2-adic basin theorem omits. Natural exact all-level structure rather than a small-instance computation.

limitations: Only dyadic moduli and exactly x²+1.
Finite verification through k=13, all-level classification uses 2-adic proof.
